mode.heading: Set-up
mode.body: Choose how the system should answer for this session. This page is for whoever is running the study; the participant starts on the next screen.
mode.stub_help: Canned, hard-coded responses. No API key needed. Use this to demo or test the full wizard.
mode.live_help: Calls the real model using the Anthropic key in backend/.env.
mode.live_warning: Live mode needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in backend/.env and the real API call implemented (it is currently a stub). Until then, choose Stubbed.

footer.exit_confirm: Are you sure you want to exit and withdraw? Your session will stop here.

consent.heading: Before we start
consent.body: Thank you for taking part. This study looks at how people ask questions of a computer system to get information out of a database. You do not need to know anything about databases or computing. The session takes about 75–90 minutes.
checkboxes: I confirm I have read and understood the information sheet.
I understand my participation is voluntary and I may stop at any time, including asking for my session recording to be deleted, without giving a reason.
I understand the session will be audio-recorded and that my data will be stored securely and anonymised.

screening.heading: A little about you
screening.body: Just a couple of quick questions before we begin. There are no right answers.

age_band.label: Which age band are you in?

sql_experience.label: How much experience do you have writing database queries (for example SQL)?

db_experience.label: How often do you work with databases or spreadsheets of records?

study_explanation.heading: What you'll be doing
study_explanation.body: You'll look at two different collections of information — think of each like a set of linked tables, the sort of thing an organisation keeps its records in. For each one, we'll ask you to come up with a couple of questions you'd genuinely want answered, in your own words. A computer system will then try to help you turn each question into a precise request and show you an answer. After each set, we'll ask what you thought. There are no right or wrong questions, and nothing here is a test of you — we're testing the system. You'll do this on your own, at your own pace.

california_schools.heading: The schools records
california_schools.body: This collection is about schools in California — each school's details, its exam (SAT) results, and figures on how many pupils qualify for free or reduced-price meals. Imagine you work in a schools district office and someone's asked you to pull together some figures.

financial.heading: The bank records
financial.body: This collection is about a bank — its customers, their accounts, the cards and loans on those accounts, and the transactions that go through them. Imagine you're an analyst at the bank answering a question from a manager.

authoring.intro: Here is the collection of records you'll be asking about. Have a quick look, then write your question below.
authoring.question_label: Your question, in your own words
authoring.nudge: Could you write a little more?

california_schools:schema_reference.task: Working in the district office, write a question that compares schools using how well their pupils did — but you decide what "did well" should mean here. Make it a question that needs you to bring schools and their results together.
california_schools:schema_reference.then: Which schools are you expecting to come back, and why?

california_schools:superlative_metric.task: Write a question asking for the top school (or top few schools) by some measure of your choosing, in a particular area of California.
california_schools:superlative_metric.then: What exactly would count as "the top" for you, and how many schools did you expect?

financial:value_reference.task: As the bank analyst, write a question about a particular kind of transaction or a particular place (a district), and which customers or accounts it involves.
financial:value_reference.then: Describe in plain words what you're trying to find.

financial:temporal_window.task: As the bank analyst, write a question about activity over some period of time that you describe in your own words (for example "recently", "last year", "over the summer"), involving accounts and their transactions.
financial:temporal_window.then: What period did you have in mind, and what answer are you expecting?

loading.heading: One moment
loading.body: The system is preparing a few questions to make sure it understands exactly what you mean…

interface.standing_instruction: Answer these to help the system understand exactly what you mean.
interface.skip_note: The system had no further questions for this one.

interface_confidence.question: Before you see the answer — do you feel this captured what you were asking for?

output.heading: Here's the answer
output.body: Based on what you told the system, here's what it found.
output.sql_heading: The request the system built for you
output.error: The system couldn't work out an answer to this one. That's useful for us to know — let's carry on.
output.empty: The request ran, but didn't return any rows.

answer_confidence.wanted_question: Is this the answer you wanted?
answer_confidence.confidence_question: How confident are you that this answer is correct?

questionnaire.heading: A few questions about that way of asking
questionnaire.sus_intro: Please say how much you agree with each statement about the system you just used.
sus_items: I think that I would like to use this system frequently.
I found the system unnecessarily complex.
I thought the system was easy to use.
I think that I would need the support of a technical person to be able to use this system.
I found the various functions in this system were well integrated.
I thought there was too much inconsistency in this system.
I would imagine that most people would learn to use this system very quickly.
I found the system very cumbersome to use.
I felt very confident using the system.
I needed to learn a lot of things before I could get going with this system.
agency_items: I felt I contributed to the answer the system gave.
The choices the system asked me to make made sense.
The interface was simple to use.
open_items: What, if anything, was confusing about this way of asking?
Was there a point where you weren't sure what the system was asking you?

debrief.heading: Last few questions
debrief.preference_question: Which of the two ways of asking did you prefer overall?
open_items: Was there ever a moment where you weren't sure whether the system had actually given you what you asked for? Tell us about it.
Anything else you'd like to flag?
debrief.final: Thanks — that's everything. You can close this window now.

withdrawn.heading: You've withdrawn
withdrawn.body: Your session has been stopped and marked withdrawn. Thank you for your time.
